case_name: T. Sareetha vs T. Venkata Subbaiah
facts_of_case: Sareetha and Venkata Subbaiah were married in 1975. They separated soon after and have been living apart for five years. Venkata Subbaiah filed a petition under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act for restitution of conjugal rights with Sareetha, which was opposed by her on jurisdictional grounds.

legal_principles.principle: The finding of fact by the lower Court cannot be disturbed by a revisional Court.
legal_principles.held: The finding of the lower Court on such a question of fact cannot be disturbed by a revisional Court.
cited_cases: Harris v. Associated Portland Cement Manufacturers Ltd., (1939) AC 71

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party to prove that a finding of fact is incorrect.
legal_principles.held: She never argued this point before the Court below nor is that plea proved to its satisfaction.
cited_cases: Woods v. Durable Suites Ltd., (1953) 1 WLR 857

outcome.final_order: The trial court's order overruling Sareetha's objection to the jurisdiction of the Cuddapah Sub-Court is set aside, and the matter is remanded back to the trial court.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
use_for_drafting: Drafting a petition for restitution of conjugal rights
